import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.67

by V. P. Shunkov

Is a periodic residually finite group finite if it satisfies the weak minimum
condition for subgroups?

Here a group is *periodic* if every element has finite order, *residually finite*
if every non-identity element lies outside some normal subgroup of finite index,
and it satisfies the *weak minimum (minimal) condition for subgroups*
(Zaicev's condition $\mathrm{Min}\text{-}\infty$) if in every descending chain of
subgroups $H_1 \geq H_2 \geq \cdots$ all but finitely many of the indices
$|H_i : H_{i+1}|$ are finite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.67»

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every $g \neq 1$ there is a normal subgroup
$N$ of finite index in $G$ with $g \notin N$. Equivalently, the intersection of all
subgroups of finite index of $G$ is trivial. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- A group $G$ satisfies the *weak minimum condition for subgroups* (Zaicev's condition
$\mathrm{Min}\text{-}\infty$) if for every descending chain of subgroups
$H_0 \geq H_1 \geq H_2 \geq \cdots$ of $G$ there is an $n$ such that the index
$|H_i : H_{i+1}|$ is finite for all $i \geq n$. Equivalently, there is no strictly descending
chain of subgroups in which every index $|H_i : H_{i+1}|$ is infinite.

The condition is imposed on all subgroups of $G$, not only on the normal ones. -/
def WeakMinCondition (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : ℕ → Subgroup G, Antitone H → ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ i ≥ n, (H (i + 1)).IsFiniteRelIndex (H i)

/-- A finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyFinite_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg ↦ ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/-- A finite group satisfies the weak minimum condition for subgroups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem weakMinCondition_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    WeakMinCondition G :=
  fun H _ ↦ ⟨0, fun i _ ↦ ⟨Subgroup.index_ne_zero_of_finite (H := (H (i + 1)).subgroupOf (H i))⟩⟩

/--
Is a periodic residually finite group finite if it satisfies the weak minimum condition
for subgroups?

That is, is every group $G$ which is periodic (`Monoid.IsTorsion G`), residually finite,
and satisfies the weak minimum condition for subgroups necessarily finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.67» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G],
      Monoid.IsTorsion G → IsResiduallyFinite G → WeakMinCondition G → Finite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.67»

modeling_decisions: The weak minimal condition is stated for arbitrary descending (Antitone) chains indexed by ℕ rather than strictly descending chains as in the decomposition note. The two are equivalent: an infinite index |Hᵢ : Hᵢ₊₁| forces Hᵢ₊₁ < Hᵢ, and a strictly descending chain with infinitely many infinite indices yields, by passing to a subsequence, one with all indices infinite. The Antitone form matches the literal textbook definition (Robinson, Zaicev).

Residual finiteness is defined elementwise with normal finite-index subgroups (g ≠ 1 → ∃ N normal of finite index, g ∉ N). This is equivalent to requiring only finite-index subgroups (take the normal core) and to the intersection of all finite-index subgroups being trivial.

Groups are quantified over Type* (universe-polymorphic), following FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1098.lean; other Kourovka files use Type. Either reading is faithful.

/-- A group $G$ is residually finite if for every $g \neq 1$ there is a normal subgroup
$N$ of finite index in $G$ with $g \notin N$, i.e. $g$ has non-trivial image in the finite
quotient $G/N$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

    WeakMinOnSubgroups G :=
  fun _ _ => ⟨0, fun _ _ => Subgroup.FiniteIndex.index_ne_zero⟩

Is a periodic residually finite group finite if it satisfies the weak minimum condition
for subgroups?

That is, is every group $G$ that is periodic (every element has finite order), residually
finite, and satisfies the weak minimum condition for subgroups necessarily finite?

    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],

  sorry
